battle.name: 巴比倫進攻海地王朝
battle.theater: 安納托利亞高原與幼發拉底河上游
battle.brief: 公元前1700年前後，巴比倫王朝自兩河中游向西北用兵，戰事見於烏加里特泥板信與《巴比倫編年史》殘片。條目所記的「海地王朝」應為「赫梯」之訛，故以安納托利亞高原的赫梯為敵方。巴比倫以攻城槌與四馬重車開路，赫梯以長矛密陣與大盾列城迎之；卡上的埃及長矛即這一代銅矛工藝的早期標本。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 巴比倫一方是幼發拉底河中游的巴比倫城邦，公元前1700年前後由阿摩利特第一王朝執政，王位在辛穆巴里特一世與其子薩姆舒迪塔那之間交替。巴比倫沒有常備軍，兵員戰時自城郊各區與盟屬城邦徵集，貴族與商人家庭按義務供出戰車手、弓手與步兵；軍令出自王庭的宮廷體系，戰時由王室指名的將領率領各支行伍，後勤靠底格里斯河與幼發拉底河的水運，以及上幼發拉底河與安納托利亞方向的銅礦供應。敵方就是條目所記的「海地王朝」，但在可靠史料中並無對應政權；學界通行的解釋是史源轉錄時把安納托利亞的「赫梯」（Hatti）訛寫成「海地」，故本條以安納托利亞高原的赫梯舊王國為對手。赫梯以哈圖沙為都，王室直屬的精銳步兵與附庸小國的徵發兵並行，軍中以長矛、雙頭斧與弓弩為主軸，車兵使用雙馬輕車。
countriesEn: The Babylonian side was the city-state of Babylon on the middle Euphrates, ruled in c. 1700 BC by the Amorite First Dynasty, the throne passing between Sin-Muballit I and his son Samsu-ditana. Babylon kept no standing army: troops were levied in time of war from the districts around the city and from the client towns, noble and merchant households furnishing chariot crews, archers and foot soldiers by obligation. Orders came out of the palace administration, and a commander named by the king led the levies in the field, while supply rode on the Tigris and the Euphrates and on copper from the upper Euphrates and the Anatolian direction. The enemy is the 'Haitian dynasty' named in the list, but no polity answers to that name in the reliable record; the standard reading is that the name is a scribal corruption of Hatti, the Anatolian kingdom, and this entry therefore takes Old Hatti, on the Anatolian plateau, as the opponent. Hatti had its capital at Hattusa, fielding a royal core of professional infantry alongside contingents raised by its client principalities, with spears, double-headed axes and bows as the axis of its armament and chariots drawn by two horses.
people: 薩姆舒迪塔那是古巴比倫第二任國王，沙姆希·阿達德一世之孫、辛穆巴里特一世之子，約公元前1625年至1595年在位，是這場衝突中唯一可以指名的主帥。他在位期間的用兵記於《巴比倫編年史》殘片，該書提到國王向赫梯方向行軍、越過幼發拉底河，卻遭逢逆轉，連王國治下的西帕爾也被掠焚；記錄同時顯示他屢次把隊伍拉出國境，卻無法穩住前進與退回路線。他的父親辛穆巴里特一世營建巴比倫外牆，並把王宮建在城北，是王朝在物質與制度上的奠基者。赫梯方面，國王哈圖西里一世在位約公元前1650年至1620年，先破哈拉美的軍隊、洗掠阿拉拉赫與哈蘇瓦，又在久攻之後攻下馬里與哈蘭，因此被後世稱為「大王」；其子穆爾西里一世更率軍直取巴比倫，把第一王朝推到終點。烏加里特的國王阿米什塔姆魯是外交中間人，兩國往來的信札多經他手，也正因如此，這場戰爭的若干關鍵細節才得以留存在泥板之上。
peopleEn: Samsu-ditana, the second king of Babylon, grandson of Shamshi-Adad I and son of Sin-Muballit I, reigned c. 1625-1595 BC and is the only commander of this conflict who can be named. His campaigning is recorded in the fragmentary Babylonian Chronicle, which describes the king marching towards the Hittites, crossing the Euphrates and then suffering a reversal, with Sippar, a city of his own realm, sacked in the process; the same text shows him taking the host out of the country again and again without being able to stabilise the road ahead or the line of retreat. His father Sin-Muballit I raised Babylon's outer wall and built the royal palace north of the city, laying the material and institutional foundation of the dynasty. On the Hittite side, Hattusili I, king c. 1650-1620 BC, first broke the army of Yamhad, sacked Alalakh and Hassuwa, and then took Mari and Harran after a long siege, whence later tradition gave him the epithet 'Great King'. His son Mursili I went further, marched on Babylon and brought the First Dynasty to its end. Ammistamru, king of Ugarit, served as diplomatic intermediary; much of the correspondence between the two courts passed through his hands, and for that reason several key details of this war survive on clay.
kits: 兵器卡上的埃及長矛屬早王朝工藝，約公元前3200年，銅或砷銅矛頭以榫或纏繩固定在木杆上，多保存於埃及乾燥的墓葬環境；同期王室畫面，如約公元前3200年的「蠍子王權杖頭」與約公元前3000年的「納爾邁調色板」，已把護衛與持矛或持權杖的步兵列入編制，說明矛是城垣與護衛的制式裝備。埃及早王朝的矛頭多為銅或砷銅，錫青銅要到中期之後才在尼羅斯河流域普遍。到公元前1700年，這門技術已傳遍近東：巴比倫與赫梯的長矛多為帶套筒的青銅矛頭，接在約兩米長的硬木杆上，槍桿修削成圓錐以便插入固定。赫梯步軍以八字形大盾（Dipylon 形制）遮蔽正面，戴頂端有長錐的青銅盔，配短劍與手斧，弓手用複合反曲弓。巴比倫以大型四馬重車作機動核心，早期重輪大車用於搬運城牆石料與木材，攻城則靠撞槌、投石與牆基地道。撞槌槌頭起初包覆銅，後改用青銅條與木材合釘，外覆濕土或炭火以抗火攻。運輸靠牛群、驢隊與河船，銅由上幼發拉底河方向運入，錫則多經長途商路自遠方輸入，安納托利亞的錫料一般認為來自高加索方向。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card belongs to the Early Dynastic craft tradition of c. 3200 BC: a copper or arsenical-copper blade hafted to a wooden shaft with a tang or binding, preserved chiefly in the dry conditions of Egyptian burials. Contemporary royal imagery, such as the Scorpion Macehead of c. 3200 BC and the Narmer Palette of c. 3000 BC, already lists guards and spearmen or standard-bearers among the establishment, showing the spear as standard equipment for walls and escorts. Egyptian early dynastic heads were mostly copper or arsenical copper, and tin bronze only became common in the Nile valley after the middle period. By 1700 BC the technique had spread across the Near East: Babylonian and Hittite spears normally carried socketed bronze heads fitted to hard wooden shafts about two metres long, the shaft dressed to a taper so that the head seated firmly. Hittite infantry covered the front with large dipylon (figure-of-eight) shields, wore bronze helmets with a tall spike, and carried short swords and hand axes, while archers used composite recurve bows. Babylon leaned on the heavy four-horse chariot as its mobile striking force, early solid-wheeled cars serving to move wall stone and timber, while siege work depended on battering rams, stone-throwers and tunnels driven under the foundations. Ram heads were first sheathed in copper and later built of bronze strips riveted to timber and covered with wet earth or embers against fire. Transport depended on oxen, donkey trains and river boats, with copper brought down from the upper Euphrates and tin reaching Mesopotamia over long-distance caravan routes, the Anatolian tin generally thought to have come from the Caucasus.
tactics: 美索不達米亞的兵季落在春末至初秋，洪水退去、道路可通之後才開拔，遠征隊伍按先鋒、主力與輜重三段拉開，首尾相隔可達數日。巴比倫的戰略是沿幼發拉底河兩岸推進，用河水輸送穀物與攻城器材，直抵敵境關口再展開圍城。攻城先以弓弩與投石壓制城頭，再以撞槌集中攻擊城門與城牆的弱段，並在牆基掘地道；守方以石壘與泥磚牆段抵抗，用箭雨與滾木消耗攻方兵員。赫梯的戰法偏向機動：輕型雙馬戰車在陣前巡行驅散敵軍，散兵以長矛列成密陣，盾牌相互搭接形成連續壁面，戰車自側翼衝擊敵陣缺口，待敵軍行列散亂後以步兵壓上。撤退多在夜裡進行，並焚燒臨近村鎮以延緩追兵。史料中巴比倫方面的失利，恰恰發生在深入敵境、回程補給線被切斷的階段，說明這支軍隊在攻勢與持久之間沒有找到平衡點。
tacticsEn: The Mesopotamian campaigning season ran from late spring into early autumn, expeditions setting out only after the flood had dropped and the roads had become passable, and the column was strung out in three echelons, vanguard, main body and baggage train, separated by days of march. Babylonian strategy was to advance along both banks of the Euphrates, using the river to carry grain and siege equipment, to reach the enemy frontier and there to invest a city by siege. The assault opened with archers and stone-throwers suppressing the walls, then concentrated the rams on the gates and the weaker stretches of the curtain, while tunnels were cut beneath the foundations; the defenders answered with stone revetments and mud-brick sections, spending arrows and falling timbers on the attackers. Hittite method leaned on mobility: light two-horse chariots ran in front of the line to disorder the enemy, the loose troops closed into dense spear ranks whose overlapping shields formed a continuous face, chariots struck the flanks and drove into the gaps, and infantry pressed on once the enemy line broke. Withdrawals were made by night, with neighbouring settlements burned to slow the pursuit. The Babylonian reverses recorded in the sources fall precisely in the phase when the army was deep in enemy country with its line of supply cut, which shows that this host never balanced attack against endurance.
data: 關於兵力，這場戰爭沒有留下任何可以核實的數字：巴比倫與赫梯的泥板和王表只留下方位、事件與稱號，沒有戰損表；後世希臘史家附會給巴比倫大軍的十萬之類的數字，來自更晚的時代與傳說，不能挪用到公元前1700年。可確定的是幾組規模性的事實。巴比倫的城防由內牆與外牆兩道組成，外牆由辛穆巴里特一世主持營建，環城周長以公里計，是當時近東最大的土木防禦工程之一；城內的廟宇群，埃薩吉拉與其基座神塔埃特曼安基，長期在使用中反覆重建，城中亦保存了數以萬計的泥板文書。赫梯首都哈圖沙在德國考古隊自1906年起主持的發掘中出土大批泥板；同一時期的書信材料主要出自1920年代末至1930年代初在烏加里特的發掘。作戰單位方面，巴比倫早期重戰車需四匹馬拉動，行李車隊可用六匹，赫梯在同一時期已改用雙馬輕車。年月方面，戰爭列表只記年份，具體月份無記載，本條填入四月，是依美索不達米亞春末開拔的兵季慣例推得，並非史料記載。年份口徑亦要交代：戰爭列表把本條編在公元前1700年，而可核實的巴比倫與赫梯交戰（《巴比倫編年史》殘片與烏加里特書信）集中在薩姆舒迪塔那在位的約公元前1625年至1595年；此處照列表編目年填寫，差異據實說明，不改機器欄位。在列表自身的編排上，本條與「海地王朝的建立」（公元前1732年，即赫梯王朝的建立）、「巴比倫的洗劫」（公元前1595年）同屬「巴比倫帝國的衰弱與滅亡」這一段，可見被記作「海地」的那一方正是安納托利亞的赫梯。
dataEn: On numbers: this war left no verifiable figures. Neither the Babylonian nor the Hittite tablets and king lists record casualty returns; they give only places, events and titles. The enormous hosts of a hundred thousand or so that later Greek historians attach to Babylonian armies belong to a later age and to legend, and cannot be carried back to 1700 BC. What can be fixed is a set of scale facts. Babylon's defences consisted of an inner and an outer wall, the outer raised under Sin-Muballit I, running many kilometres around the city and forming one of the largest earth-and-brick works of the ancient Near East. The temple quarter inside the city, Esagila and the ziggurat Etemenanki that stood on it, was repeatedly rebuilt while still in use, and tens of thousands of clay tablets were stored in the town. The Hittite capital Hattusa yielded a great mass of tablets in the excavations begun by the German expedition in 1906; the correspondence of the same period comes chiefly from the excavations at Ugarit in the late 1920s and early 1930s. On the scale of equipment, the early Babylonian war chariot needed four horses, baggage teams up to six, and the Hittites had already moved to light two-horse cars in this period. On dating, the war list gives only the year, no month is documented, and the month entered here, April, is inferred from the normal spring opening of the Mesopotamian campaigning season rather than from any source. The year itself needs a note too: the list files this entry under 1700 BC, while the Babylonian-Hittite clashes that can actually be documented, the Babylonian Chronicle fragments and the Ugarit letters, cluster in the reign of Samsu-ditana, c. 1625-1595 BC. The catalogue year is kept here and the discrepancy stated rather than the machine field changed. In the list's own arrangement this entry sits in the same stretch as the establishment of the Hittite dynasty (1732 BC) and the sack of Babylon (1595 BC), all of them sections of the fall of the Babylonian empire, and the side the list calls Haiti is plainly the Hittites of Anatolia.
cause: 先講名稱。戰爭列表收錄的這條目名為「巴比倫進攻海地王朝」，但「海地」在這裡對不上任何公元前1700年的政權：加勒比海的伊斯帕尼奧拉島當時屬泰諾人的村落社會，沒有王朝、沒有城牆、沒有文字，也沒有青銅冶煉與馬匹，兩河的編年史更從未記載過跨越大西洋的遠征。合理的解釋是史源轉錄的訛字，把安納托利亞的「赫梯」（Hatti）寫成「海地」，中譯再把「赫梯王國」處理成「海地王朝」。所以本條把戰爭的實體當作巴比倫第一王朝末年對安納托利亞方向的用兵。真正可考的起因有三層。第一是王朝的地理處境：巴比倫卡在幼發拉底河中游，國界夾在阿摩利特人的舊土與北方高地之間，向北是亞述，向西是阿姆魯與哈拉美，向東則是巴比倫自認應當收攏的赫梯邊境。第二是赫梯的西進：哈圖西里一世把國家推向幼發拉底河上游，攻破馬里與哈蘭之後，赫梯貴族要求把勢力再壓到河中游，正撞上巴比倫的城牆與商路。第三是原料與交通：銅料與木材的取得，往北方口岸的商隊安全，都要在壓力下重新談判，於是邊境衝突成了必然。而在戰爭列表自身的編排裡，這條「巴比倫進攻海地王朝」正是「巴比倫帝國的衰弱與滅亡」這一段中的一節：前有「海地王朝的建立」（公元前1732年），後有「巴比倫的洗劫」（公元前1595年），所謂「海地王朝」就是這條編年線上被記作「海地」的那一方——安納托利亞的赫梯。
causeEn: First the name. The war list records this entry as 'Babylon attacks the Haitian dynasty', but nothing in 1700 BC corresponds to 'Haiti'. In the Caribbean, the island of Hispaniola held a village society of the Taíno, with no dynasty, no walls, no writing, no bronze smelting and no horses, and no Mesopotamian chronicle records an expedition across the Atlantic. The reasonable explanation is a scribal corruption: Hatti, in Anatolia, was written as Haiti, and the Chinese rendering then turned 'kingdom of Hatti' into 'Haitian dynasty'. This entry therefore treats the war as the campaigns of the late Babylonian First Dynasty towards Anatolia. The documented causes run in three layers. First, dynastic geography: Babylon sat on the middle Euphrates with its frontier pinched between Amorite country to the west and the highlands to the north and east, Assyria beyond, Amurru and Yamhad to the west, and the Hittite borderlands to the east which Babylon considered its own to absorb. Second, Hittite pressure: Hattusili I pushed the state up the Euphrates, and after the fall of Mari and Harran the Hittite nobility sought the middle Euphrates, where Babylonian walls and caravan roads stood in the way. Third, raw materials and traffic: the supply of copper and timber, and the safety of the caravan roads to the northern emporia, all had to be renegotiated under pressure, and a clash of frontiers followed. The list's own arrangement says as much: this entry, 'Babylon attacks the Haitian dynasty', is one section of 'the fall of the Babylonian empire', between the establishment of the Hittite dynasty (1732 BC) and the sack of Babylon (1595 BC). The dynasty the list calls Haiti is on this chronology none other than the Hittites of Anatolia.
impact: 短期看，巴比倫第一王朝的西境防線被打開：辛穆巴里特一世營建的外牆與薩姆舒迪塔那的遠征都沒有守住北方的緩衝，薩姆舒迪塔那之後，巴比倫在亞述與赫梯兩面受壓，國勢由攻轉守，最終在約公元前1595年被穆爾西里一世攻破，王朝終結，王室成員帶著神像遷往敘利亞方面的據點。長期看，這幾十年給近東留下三樣東西。一是把赫梯推上區域強權的位置，安納托利亞的冶金與城防技術在隨後數百年成為主角，亞述在巴比倫崩潰後接管了這片空出的版圖。二是巴比倫的制度遺產，法律、官制、灌溉與銅銀重量單位隨第一王朝的流散進入敘利亞與亞述，後來被整理成文字，即《漢謨拉比法典》，成為兩河流域以外影響最遠的一套法規範本。三是兵器工藝的世代更替：這場戰爭所用的長矛仍是銅矛加木杆的早期形態，套筒青銅矛頭才剛出現，工具與冶金的進步其後把矛尖推向鐵質，卡上那件早王朝的埃及長矛因此成為「第一代金屬矛」在博物館中的標準標本。
impactEn: In the short term the western shield of the Babylonian First Dynasty was opened. Neither the outer wall raised by Sin-Muballit I nor the expeditions of Samsu-ditana held the northern buffer, and after Samsu-ditana the kingdom was pressed from Assyria and from Hatti at once, turned from attack to defence, and was finally taken by Mursili I in c. 1595 BC. The dynasty ended, and members of the royal house carried the gods of the city away to their strongholds in Syria. In the long term the decades left the Near East three inheritances. They lifted Hatti into the position of regional power: Anatolian metallurgy and fortification became the leading craft of the following centuries, and Assyria, left the free hand by Babylon's collapse, took over the vacated terrain. They dispersed the institutions of Babylon: law, administration, irrigation and the copper and silver weight system travelled with the First Dynasty's exiles into Syria and Assyria, were later written down as the Code of Hammurabi, and became the most far-reaching legal code outside Mesopotamia itself. And they marked a generational change in weapons: the spears of this war were still copper blades on wooden shafts, socketed bronze heads had only just appeared, and the advance of tools and metallurgy later carried the head into iron, which is why the Early Dynastic Egyptian spear on the card stands in the museums as the standard reference for the first generation of metal spear.
result: 結局沒有留下一場決定性的會戰紀錄，戰爭以巴比倫方面的失敗收場。線索來自三處：其一，《巴比倫編年史》殘片提到國王向赫梯方向用兵，以及西帕爾被毀，說明深入之後的補給與撤退出了問題；其二，烏加里特出土的書信中，哈圖西里一世致阿米什塔姆魯的信直接提到巴比倫王對西帕爾的破壞，並轉向烏加里特求取銅料，說明巴比倫的攻勢在史料中是被赫梯一方當作威脅描述的；其三，赫梯王表把哈圖西里一世在任期的最大功業記為攻下馬里與哈蘭，而巴比倫方面的城市損失未見於敵方記載。就結果而言，巴比倫沒有從這場戰爭得到任何持久的收益，遠征隊伍、牲畜與攻城器材大多耗在途程與敗退之中；赫梯則把邊界推到幼發拉底河中游，換來控制高地的時間差。約公元前1620年，馬里與哈蘭陷落，阿拉美與阿姆魯的聯盟瓦解；約公元前1595年，穆爾西里一世入巴比倫城，第一王朝告終，而「海地王朝」這個名字，從未在任何史書中出現過。
resultEn: The war left no record of any decisive battle, and it ended in Babylonian failure. The evidence comes from three places. First, the fragment of the Babylonian Chronicle speaks of the king's march towards the Hittites and of the destruction of Sippar, which points to a breakdown of supply and of the withdrawal. Second, among the letters from Ugarit is one in which Hattusili I writes to Ammistamru, mentions the Babylonian king's ruin of Sippar, and turns to Ugarit for copper, so that the Babylonian offensive appears in the sources as a threat described from the Hittite side. Third, the Hittite king lists give the greatest achievement of Hattusili I's reign as the taking of Mari and Harran, while the Babylonian urban losses do not appear in the enemy's account. As for the outcome, Babylon drew no lasting gain from this war: the expedition's troops, draught animals and siege equipment were largely spent on the march and in the retreat, while Hatti moved its frontier to the middle Euphrates and bought itself time in the highlands. Mari and Harran fell c. 1620 BC and the alliance of Yamhad and Amurru came apart; c. 1595 BC Mursili I entered Babylon, the First Dynasty ended, and the name 'Haitian dynasty' never appeared in any historical record at all.
